findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which existing check_*.py guard the detector reuses/mirrors (e.g. check_config_reads.py's AST+escape-marker shape and check_criteria_vocabulary.py's allowlist idiom), following the check()/main() contract and the named-gate-step wiring in _build-and-test.yml + .pre-commit-config.yaml — or justify why a new harness/escape-hatch mechanism is warranted over these established patterns.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'scripts/ or CI lint module implementing the detector + workflow wiring' — no reference to any existing guard.

scripts/check_config_reads.py (ticket 6754): AST-level check over src/rebar with a '# read-via: <pointer>' escape marker, wired into CI 'alongside existing gates' — the exact detector+escape-hatch+CI shape the plan proposes.

scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py: a near-identical sibling — a repo-wide text-pattern scanner that confines a deprecated pattern to reviewed records via a tab-delimited path/count/reason allowlist file, with parse_args/main and dataclass match records.

.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml wires these as named gate steps (e.g. 'Config-read gate', 'server.json env-contract drift gate'); .pre-commit-config.yaml wires local check-only hooks — an established wiring pattern the plan does not name.
ANTI-FP note: this is a well-trodden lint/guard pattern, so no external prior-art search is needed and no novel architecture is being introduced; the finding is scoped to in-repo reuse.
findings.finding: The plan proposes a comment/docstring hygiene scanner + escape hatch + CI wiring without referencing the repo's established check_*.py guard convention, which is directly-applicable prior art it appears to be reinventing.
findings.location: Approach step (2) and Scope bullet 'scripts/ or CI lint module implementing the detector + workflow wiring'
scenarios: Implementer writes a bespoke scan/allowlist/CI-wiring harness from scratch, diverging from the check()/main() contract and the named-gate-step convention every other guard follows.

The 'context: external' escape hatch is implemented as a novel mechanism when the repo already has two escape-hatch idioms ('# read-via:' inline marker; criteria-vocabulary tab-delimited allowlist) that could be adopted or consciously rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / reuse' note to the Approach: the detector adopts the in-repo guard convention (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py with check()/main(), wired as a named step in _build-and-test.yml and as a check-only pre-commit hook), mirroring check_config_reads.py's AST-docstring + escape-marker design and reusing check_criteria_vocabulary.py's tab-delimited allowlist for the 'context: external' escape hatch (or explicitly justify choosing the inline-comment escape over the allowlist file).
